newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares gallop to fourth record high.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares gallop to fourth record high.

text.p: Egyptian shares romped to a fourth straight high on Wednesday as gains in the cement and milling sectors maintained the market's upward momentum.
The boom, which began late last month and slackened only for a few days, has continued right into the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, despite shorter working hours at the exchange.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 5.5 points to end at 352.08. Turnover was an unusually heavy 142.27 million pounds ($41.8 million) as the state sold a majority stake worth 93.49 million in Misr Free Shops through the bourse.

The state privatised 66.8 percent of the duty-free goods firm at the end of an auction which fixed the sale price at 40 pounds a share. The amount sold was more than twice the 1.05 million shares the state had originally offered, the CMA said.
Most of the day's remaining turnover came from trading in the favourite cement and milling sectors.

Amriyah Cement was the day's most active share, rising 0.50 pounds to 78. Helwan Portland Cement was also among the sector's best performers, gaining 1.5 pounds to 78.5 on turnover worth more than seven million pounds.
Suez Cement also did well and ended the day 1.48 pounds higher at 72.5 pounds.

The popular milling firms also saw a lot of trading on Wednesday and partially privatised Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the day's biggest gainer, rising 5 percent or 4.98 pounds to 104.53. The state sold off part of its stake in the firm in September at 40 pounds a share.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills rose 3.2 pounds to 87.2 in heavy trading while Central Egypt Flour Mills gained 2.9 to 60.9 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 572.39 points from 557.95 on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 236.03 from 233.83.
Of the 77 shares traded, 44 gained, 8 lost and 25 ended the day unchanged.
